description: first_sql_keyword's '' covers no token, non-word first token and TokenError; it also returns any unquoted identifier while called a keyword.
Scope-analysis fallback log records only the exception type at INFO; matches criterion, missing context.
Empty-SQL check uses str.strip(), so comment-only SQL reaches the runner and with read_only off is reported as a green '1 row(s) affected'. Pre-existing.
first_sql_keyword and is_read_shaped tokenize the same SQL twice (same in is_introspection_query).

src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py lines 73-78: the tool and the runner each decide read vs write; READ_RESULT_ATTR covers only the runner-read direction, write-branch rows_affected frames carry no marker, and RunSqlTool.dialect is public, defaults to None and is not validated at construction (a misspelled dialect logs a WARNING twice per execute and falls back to no dialect). Not reachable through build_agent wiring.

docs/internal/agent/tool-scratch-storage.md lines 7 and 14 say only is_read_shaped read-shaped statements get a result table and only non-read-shaped ones get the row-count summary; run_sql.py line 78 also builds the table when the runner frame carries READ_RESULT_ATTR, which tests pin.

src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py lines 91-94: is_read_shaped docstring still says 'Cheap first-token check' although first_sql_keyword tokenizes the whole statement and a TokenError anywhere gives '' and False.

docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md line 302 says query_type is the leading SQL keyword and '' when no keyword leads; first_sql_keyword also returns an unquoted identifier uppercased (test_unquoted_identifier_is_returned pins 'foo bar' -> 'FOO').

docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md line 302: the query_type bullet says it is '' when no keyword leads the statement, but a bare-identifier-led statement yields that identifier uppercased, as readonly.py lines 50-51 and test_unquoted_identifier_is_returned show.
transport.md line 123 omits the read_result route to the CSV write.
is_read_shaped docstring names only the SQL runners as caller; RunSqlTool.execute now also uses it.
TestSqliteRunnerCommentLedRowCap docstring only records past behavior.
No test runs a marked frame through RowCapRunner truncation; the mark survives only via pandas attrs propagation through iloc/copy.
first_sql_keyword returns "" on TokenError without logging; with read_only off a read sqlglot cannot tokenize is reported as row(s) affected with no trace.
Comment-led WITH ... UPDATE routing with read_only off (criterion text) is not pinned by a test; #316 tracks it.

The release note says query_database now gets the rows of every read the agent runs, but with read_only off EXPLAIN, VALUES, SQLite PRAGMA, Postgres INSERT ... RETURNING and tokenizer-rejected reads still get a row count with their rows dropped.
_cte_reference_ids relies on normalize_identifiers rewriting in place and matches nodes by id(); a copying normalization would silently exclude nothing.
